sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *afirmar* from B2 Unit 18, and the other reporting verbs (*advertir*, *recordar*, *señalar*, *negar*): they say not only that someone spoke but how. A fact the speaker states takes the indicative; a claim that is rejected, a suggestion or an order takes the subjunctive. They are what you need to report what experts and defenders of a language say.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: Varios lingüistas señalan que el quechua pierde hablantes jóvenes.
*señalar que* + indicative: a fact they point out
Los defensores de la lengua afirman que muchos artistas la usan.
Los lingüistas recuerdan que se asoció con la discriminación.
*recordar que* + indicative: reminds of a fact
Nadie niega que el quechua sea una lengua viva.
*negar que* + subjunctive: a claim that is rejected

items.spanish: Varios lingüistas señalan que el quechua pierde hablantes jóvenes en las ciudades.
items.english: Several linguists point out that Quechua is losing young speakers in the cities.

items.spanish: Los defensores de la lengua afirman que algunos artistas jóvenes la usan en su música.
items.english: The defenders of the language say that some young artists use it in their music.

items.spanish: Los lingüistas recuerdan que durante mucho tiempo el quechua se asoció con la discriminación.
items.english: Linguists remind us that for a long time Quechua was associated with discrimination.

items.spanish: Nadie niega que el quechua sea una lengua viva.
items.english: Nobody denies that Quechua is a living language.

sections.content: Name who says it: a reporting verb makes the source clear, so the reader can see what is a fact and what is a claim. Tense follows B2 Unit 17: after a past verb, shift the tense back.
